title: Casualty Claims Handler
description:
A renowned National Loss Adjusting Organisation are now seeking an experienced Liability Claims Handler to join their specialist Casualty Liability Team.
- You will handle a variety of specialist Liability claims, predominantly EL & PL and Third-Party Property Damage losses.
- You will manage and be responsible for your own caseload of losses, being part of a dedicated team you will play a vital part of the business by providing an exceptional claims service to key clients.
- Due to growth and expansion this will be an exciting time to join where you will be offered the opportunity to progress and develop long-term.

Key responsibilities:
- Handle predominantly EL & PL claims through to settlement
- Manage your own dedicated caseload of Casualty claims and handling enquiries in relation to policy indemnity, legal liability and quantum
- Liaise with the Insurer, Policyholder and Broker
- Investigate allocated claims, looking at evidence and liaising with all relevant parties and determining liability
- Where appropriate refer to a field adjuster for site investigation to establish how the loss occurred

- Determine appropriate action for resolution

- Liability/Casualty Claims handling experience specifically EL & PL (Personal Injury) including Property Damage within the Loss Adjusting, Insurance or Legal Industry
- Experience of handling your caseload of claims through to settlement
- The ability to value an injury loss
- Experience of handling defendant losses
- Excellent communication skills both verbal and written
- Good planning and organisational skills
- Solid IT skills and be able to use multiple in-house systems
- Insurance Industry Qualifications or working towards desirable

Benefits on offer:
- Remote or hybrid depending on location, 35 hours per week Monday to Friday
- Flexible benefits including holiday purchase plan and the opportunity to purchase health cash and BUPA dental plan, flexible working, 5% pension, life assurance 4 x, enhanced maternity, paternity, and adoption pay, discounts with UK retailers, wellbeing hub and many more

title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
Customer Service Advisor

Red Recruitment is recruiting Customer Service Advisors in Leeds city centre to join our client, an award-winning customer management company that has achieved GOLD awards from both Investors in People and Investors in Customers.

In this role, you will provide telephone support to enforcement agents attending customers properties in relation to outstanding utility debt. You will complete structured fact-finding checks, review account information and ensure the correct legal, regulatory and operational procedures have been followed before any action is taken.

You will help ensure every case is handled fairly, accurately and with appropriate consideration for the customer s individual circumstances.

Benefits and Package for a Customer Service Advisor:
- Salary: £26,227.50 per annum
- Hours: Full-time, Monday to Friday, working hours between 8am and 6pm
- Contract Type: Permanent
- Location: Leeds city centre
- Free parking
- Health and wellbeing programme
- Monthly bonus scheme
- Internal recognition schemes with financial awards
- 33 days annual leave, including bank holidays and your birthday
- Social events, including Summer and Christmas parties
- Full support and training provided
- Career progression opportunities

Key Responsibilities of a Customer Service Advisor:
- Provide telephone and operational support to enforcement agents attending customers properties
- Complete a structured fact-finding process with agents during live property visits
- Review customer accounts, outstanding debt information and previous actions taken
- Check that the relevant legal, regulatory and company procedures have been followed correctly
- Confirm that all required notices, documentation and warrant-related checks have been completed
- Identify factors that could affect how a case should proceed, including vulnerability, affordability concerns or a change of occupier
- Provide guidance to field agents on the appropriate next steps in line with company procedures
- Stop or escalate cases where information is incomplete, procedures have not been followed or additional support is required
- Monitor live cases and provide operational support to help visits progress safely and appropriately
- Escalate complex, sensitive or high-risk cases to specialist teams when required

Key Skills and Experience of a Customer Service Advisor:
- Previous experience in customer service, contact centre, operations support, collections or a regulated environment
- Experience supporting vulnerable customers or handling sensitive situations would be advantageous
- Strong questioning and fact-finding skills, with the confidence to obtain accurate information
- Excellent verbal communication skills and the ability to provide clear guidance over the telephone
- Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow structured procedures accurately
- Good judgement, with the confidence to challenge, stop or escalate a case when necessary
- Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
- Experience within utilities, debt recovery, revenue protection, financial services or another regulated sector would be beneficial

If you are interested in this position and have the relevant skills and experience required, please apply now!

title: HR Assistant
description:
Sewell Wallis is delighted to be working with a leading global professional services organisation in Leeds, West Yorkshire, that is looking to recruit an HR Assistant to join their busy and collaborative HR team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced HR Administrator or HR Assistant looking for their next step within a well-established, forward-thinking business. You'll be joining a fast-paced team where you'll gain exposure to a wide variety of HR processes and have the opportunity to develop your skills and career.

What will you be doing?

This is a varied HR role supporting the full employee life-cycle, with a particular focus on HR administration and ensuring processes are completed accurately and within deadlines.

You'll be responsible for:
- Managing the full on-boarding process for new starters, including right to work checks, issuing offers and contracts, completing on-boarding activities and setting up employee records.
- Managing the off-boarding process for leavers and ensuring everything is completed within payroll deadlines.
- Processing changes to terms and conditions, including preparing letters and communicating changes to employees.
- Maintaining accurate and up-to-date employee information on the HR system.
- Processing changes such as cost centre moves, reporting line changes and contractual amendments.
- Responding to day-to-day HR queries, including maternity, paternity and flexible working.
- Supporting the wider HR team with projects and process improvement initiatives.
- Providing general HR team support, including preparing PowerPoint presentations, taking meeting notes and assisting with day-to-day activities.
- Ensuring all HR administration is completed accurately, efficiently and confidentially.

What skills are we looking for?

We're looking for someone who has previous experience working within an HR Administrator or HR Assistant role and is keen to continue developing their career within HR.

You'll ideally have:
- Previous experience within HR administration or HR support.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- An understanding of UK Right to Work requirements.
- Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage a high-volume workload.
- The confidence to work independently and take ownership of your workload.
- Experience using HR systems - Workday experience would be advantageous.
- Good knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word, PowerPoint and SharePoint.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- A proactive, adaptable and positive approach.
- The ability to work well as part of a busy and collaborative team.

What's on offer?
- 25,000 - 30,000 salary
- Hybrid working + Benefits package
- The opportunity to join a global and highly respected organisation
- A supportive and collaborative HR team
- A varied role with exposure to the full employee life-cycle
- Excellent opportunity for career development and progression

If you're an HR Administrator or HR Assistant looking for a new opportunity with a business that can offer variety, development and hybrid working, this could be a great next step for you.

To apply, please apply below or contact Jemima for more information.

To apply please send your CV, quoting our reference and specifying which website you saw this position advertised on. Due to the high volume of applications please accept that if we have not responded to your application within seven days, your application has not been successful. Sewell Wallis is a specialist recruitment company with a vast amount of experience in our industry we offer permanent, temporary and interim recruitment support for accounting and finance, human resources and business support positions. We recruit at all levels within finance from Purchase Ledger Administrator and Credit Controller level through to Financial Controller and Director positions. With offices in Sheffield and Leeds, we are well situated to cover all of South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire and Manchester. Please visit our website for more information on accountancy and finance jobs and human resources or business support positions.

title: Internal Sales Administrator
description:
Breedon Group plc is a leading vertically integrated construction materials group in Great Britain, Ireland, and the USA. We're dedicated to providing high-quality materials and services for the construction industry, with a commitment to safety, sustainability, and innovation. Joining Breedon means becoming part of a team that values excellence and is committed to making a positive impact.

Position Overview:
We are currently seeking an Internal Sales Administrator based at our Leeds concrete plant.

You will be a key member of the sales team focused on the sales of construction material products.

Key Responsibilities

You will be responsible for dealing with inbound enquiries from customers, offering sales admin support to Territory Sales Managers and pricing/chasing/winning orders.

To positively represent the Breedon brand, the Internal Sales Representative offers our customers an excellent and professional service.

The key responsibilities of the role are as follows:
- Ensure all phones are answered in a timely manner, and enquiries recorded.
- Raise quotations and price them within the tolerances agreed by the TSM responsible for the area.
- Add relevant notes to enquiries detailing any correspondence with the customer.
- Process order acknowledgments when POs received and confirm via notes on Excalibur.
- Administration of the Cash Sales Process including the recording of the data for the Purchase Ledger Team.
- Generate weekly reports for the Area Sales Manager, reporting key sales data and any significant enquiries.
- Actively seek and identify opportunities to sell additional products and upsell on the initial enquiry received.
- Work pro-actively to identify new or declining customers, sites and opportunities.
- You may on occasion be required to cover other departments.

Skills, Knowledge & Expertise
- Focus on the customer relationship - maintain good customer relations and actively build new ones
- Desire to succeed and build on customer base, upselling a range of products to ensure that Breedon succeeds and is the solution of choice for appropriate building projects
- Peruse personal development of our product range
- Effective time management, adhering to administrative policies and procedures
- Attention to detail to ensure sales data produced is accurate

Job Benefits

A tailored, competitive salary
Company Pension Scheme
25 days annual leave, plus bank holidays on top
Share Saver Scheme participation
Company Life Assurance Scheme
Access to our Employee Assistance Programme for health and wellbeing support
Discounts on a wide range of products through our employee benefits platform
Broad learning opportunities and career progression pathways

Diversity Statement:
At Breedon Group, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where diversity is valued. We believe in equality of opportunity for all and encourage applications from a diverse range of candidates.

Join Us:
If you're looking for a role that challenges you, offers progression, and contributes to building better futures, we'd love to hear from you. This position is an opportunity to grow your career within a supportive and dynamic environment at Breedon Group.

Application Process:
Ready to make a meaningful difference? Apply now by submitting your CV and cover letter. We look forward to considering your application and potentially welcoming you to our team.

title: Administrator
description: THE PHARMACIST NETWORK Administrator Job Description Reports to: Business Operations Coordinator Direct reports: None Location: Newcastle, Hybrid Working pattern: Full-time, Monday-Friday 9am-5pm Salary: £26,000 £27,000 The Administrator keeps the day-to-day administration of the TPN central team running. It is a broad, hands-on support role: managing shared inboxes and correspondence, maintaining accurate records across TPN's systems, preparing documentation, and coordinating the routine processes that keep a busy operations function moving. The role suits someone organised and IT literate who is comfortable owning routine work end to end, spotting when something has been missed, and keeping records clean without being chased. Key accountabilities: Manage TPN's shared administrative inboxes triaging enquiries, responding to routine correspondence, and routing what needs a specialist to the right person. Maintain accurate, current records across TPN's systems and shared drives data entry, file management, version control, and routine housekeeping. Prepare and format documents, templates, reports, and correspondence to a consistent standard. Support the compliance administration around TPN's workforce collating and filing documentation, tracking what is outstanding, and flagging gaps for the responsible manager. Coordinate meetings and diary logistics scheduling, room and video setup, circulating papers, and taking and distributing notes where required. Provide administrative support to the wider central team on projects and recurring operational tasks. Handle sensitive and confidential information in line with GDPR and TPN's data handling requirements. Contribute to improving administrative processes surfacing what is slow, duplicated, or manual, and helping tidy it up. This list is not exhaustive; the role may include other administrative responsibilities as the central team develops. Skills and experience Essential skills: Organisation and prioritisation managing a varied workload across competing requests without dropping detail IT literacy confident across Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, SharePoint) and quick to pick up new systems Accuracy and attention to detail, particularly in data entry and record keeping Clear written and verbal communication, including professional correspondence with colleagues and external contacts Discretion and confidentiality when handling personal and sensitive information Self-direction and initiative - comfortable organising and managing your own workload. Essential experience: Prior administrative experience in an office, operations, or business support setting Experience maintaining records or databases with a high standard of accuracy Experience managing a shared inbox or handling routine correspondence on behalf of a team Desirable: Healthcare, primary care, pharmacy, or NHS-adjacent experience Experience supporting a compliance, HR, or recruitment administration process Familiarity with CRM, ATS, or workflow systems (TPN is moving onto the Zoho ecosystem) Experience working in a hybrid team across multiple sites
